newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ukraine's Kuchma in Moscow for talks with Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma in Moscow for talks with Yeltsin.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Thursday arrived in Moscow for talks with ailing Russian leader Boris Yeltsin which looked set to be overshadowed by the flare-up of a row over the Black Sea fleet.

Shortly before the talks were due to start, Russia's lower house of parliament warned Ukraine that Moscow would never hand over control of the Crimean port of Sevastopol, home to the disputed Black Sea fleet.
The State Duma made the warning in an appeal passed one day after deputies voted overwhelmingly to halt division between Russia and Ukraine of the 600-vessel fleet.

"It is not just presidents and prime ministers who suffer from the lack of understanding between Russia and Ukraine in some areas, but the people of both countries as well," Interfax news agency quoted Kuchma as saying.
"There are questions, they have to be solved, and let there be goodwill on both sides," he said.

Kuchma said the two countries were closer than ever to signing a major political treaty on future relations, but that he had come to Moscow mainly to find out how Yeltsin was feeling before heart surgery planned for next month.
"(The meeting) will not comprise deep discussions of all the problems affecting relations between Ukraine and Russia. I just want to have a chat with Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin)," Kuchma said.

The Duma said a Soviet decree of 1948 which put Sevastopol under Moscow's direct rule was still valid and that Russia, as the successor state to the Soviet Union, therefore still had jurisdiction over the port.
